# T3 — Do imputed monthly changes track real local price movements? (Task 2.2, local)

*Generated by `analysis/notes.py` from `outputs/tables/T3_local_changes.csv` and `T3b_spikes.csv`.*

**Claim 1 (spikes; no noise correction needed).** Of 138 persistent survey price jumps above 10% in the clean hold-out (level shift retained ≥ 50% the next month), the published imputed series moved ≥ 5% in the same direction in 29 (21%).

| item | pairs_with_next | spikes | caught | share_caught |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lentils | 1289 | 48 | 7 | 0.146 |
| oil | 1489 | 33 | 6 | 0.182 |
| rice | 619 | 6 | 0 | 0.000 |
| wheat_flour | 1378 | 51 | 16 | 0.314 |
| ALL | 4775 | 138 | 29 | 0.210 |

**Claim 2 (local correlation).** In the headline sample (cross-sectional stratum, both months imputed), the correlation between imputed and surveyed local changes is 0.10–0.44 with own-release means removed and -0.13–0.10 with within-month demeaning; most 95% intervals include zero (n = 74–117 pairs per item). Gate G1 and the noise correction are in T1.

**Method.** Local change = monthly log change minus the observed-market mean of the same release (own_mu) or minus the evaluation-sample month mean (within_month). β_MZ = slope of observed on imputed local change (the multiplier on regression coefficients when imputed local changes stand in for real ones). ρ* = corr/√rel with rel from Table 1 (A_main, matched to pairs including stale zero changes; and the 1%-trimmed variant). CIs: two-way pigeonhole bootstrap, 500 draws.

**Caveats.** Exploratory. Small samples; wide intervals. Mixed pairs (t−1 observed) share the survey value at t−1 with the truth. Spike detection needs the survey value at t+1, which conditions on future observation.

**Files.** `outputs/tables/T3_local_changes.csv`, `T3b_spikes.csv`; script `analysis/t3_local_changes.py`.
